title: Slack
summary: Workspace chat at scale: persistent WebSocket gateways, channel-partitioned message storage, and pub/sub fan-out to the online members of each channel.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Send and receive messages in channels and DMs in real time
Message history with infinite scroll; threads and reactions
Delivery to online members < 500 ms p99
Messages never lost; order preserved within a channel
Workspaces up to 500k members; channels up to 100k members

blocks.text: Real Slack routes messages through channel servers and gateway servers and stores data in MySQL sharded with Vitess; this design follows that shape and generalizes where details aren't public.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: Writes are modest at 70k a second; the expensive part is fan-out, about a million deliveries a second, and holding 20 million persistent connections.

POST /api/chat.postMessage   { channel, text, threadTs?, clientMsgId }   -> { ts }
GET  /api/conversations.history?channel&cursor&limit=50
WS   wss://gateway/…  server → client events: message, reaction_added, typing, presence_change
     client → server: ping, typing, mark_read

head: Entity
Key
Notes
rows: ts = time-ordered unique ID; sharded by channel_id
Replies stored like messages with parent ts

blocks.text: Sharding messages by `channel_id` keeps one channel's history on one shard, so `history` is a single range scan. Workspace-level sharding was Slack's original model; very large workspaces forced moving to finer-grained (channel) sharding.

blocks.caption: Write via API, fan-out via channel servers to the gateways holding recipients

items: Client POSTs the message with a `clientMsgId` (idempotency).
Message API writes to the channel's shard and gets the `ts`.
It hands the message to the channel server that owns the channel (consistent hashing).
The channel server knows which gateways have subscribers for this channel and pushes to each.
Gateways write the event down each member's socket; offline members get mobile push via Kafka workers.
When a client connects, its gateway subscribes to the channel servers for all of that user's channels.
Channel server keeps `channel → set of gateways` (not users), so one message to a 10k-member channel becomes ~a few hundred gateway sends, and gateways fan out locally.
Large channels: rate-limit announcements, batch reactions, and send lightweight 'new message' hints to clients that then fetch.

blocks.title: Key idea
blocks.text: Fan out to gateways, not users. It turns O(members) network hops into O(gateways), and each gateway loops locally over its sockets.

sections.title: Deep dive: ordering, delivery and reconnects

items: Order within a channel comes from the single writer: the shard assigns a monotonically increasing `ts`.
Clients render optimistically with `clientMsgId` and reconcile when the server echoes the event.
On reconnect, the client sends its last seen `ts` per channel and fetches the gap via history API, so missed WebSocket events are never lost.
At-least-once to the socket; clients dedupe by `ts`.

blocks.title: Trap
blocks.text: Don't rely on the WebSocket as the source of truth. It's a notification pipe; history in the DB is the truth.

items: Presence is derived from connection state and heartbeats; stored in an in-memory store with TTL.
Only push presence for users visible to a client (DM list, open channel), not the whole workspace: a 100k workspace can't broadcast every status change.
Typing indicators are ephemeral pub/sub, never persisted, and dropped under load.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Clients reconnect with jittered backoff to another gateway, fetch gaps
Jitter, connection admission control, cached boot payload
Dedicated channel server, coalesce updates, read-only announcement mode
Vitess primary failover; queue writes briefly
Acceptable seconds; index async from Kafka

head: Decision
Chose
Gave up
rows: Simpler horizontal store vs familiar relational tooling

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: Fan-out via gateways, ordering + reconnect, presence scoping.

items.title: Wrap-up
items.text: Reconnect storms, hot channels, delivery latency metrics.

items.a: Store `last_read_ts` per user-channel; unread = messages with ts > last_read_ts, counted lazily and cached; badges update via events.
Index messages from Kafka into Elasticsearch partitioned by workspace; enforce channel membership filters at query time.
Pin a workspace's shards to a region; gateways in other regions proxy to it.
Write an edit event with the same ts; fan out like a message; history returns the latest version.

items.q: Why not Kafka for the real-time path?
items.a: Kafka adds latency and isn't built for per-user socket routing; it's used for async side effects (push, search, analytics).

items: Gateways hold sockets; channel servers fan out.
Fan out to gateways, not users.
Shard messages by channel_id; ts gives order.
clientMsgId makes sends idempotent.
Reconnect → fetch gap by last ts.
Presence only for visible users.
Kafka for push, search, analytics.
